processing: Made as other sheng pu-erh usually is: withered, pan-fired, rolled and sun-dried into maocha, then sold loose or pressed, with no ripening pile.
harvest_season: As with other Yunnan sheng, spring is the prized picking and autumn is a cheaper, softer second choice.
appearance_dry: Long, dark olive-green large leaf with some silvery buds, typical of Yunnan sun-dried maocha.
appearance_liquor: Clear golden yellow when young, deepening with age as sheng does.
appearance_wet: Thick olive-green leaves that open fully, as is usual for large-leaf Yunnan material.
taste_profile: Tasting notes from drinkers describe a firm, full, rather wild tea whose bitterness clears quickly into a sweet aftertaste; little independent tasting evidence exists.

brewing.notes: Rinse briefly. Keep early steeps short with young cakes, as with any strong sheng.

vintage_note: Sold like other sheng pu-erh, by harvest year, usually as spring material from named old trees or the wider village area. Young cakes are drunk within a few years or stored for ageing. Check which Bangwai is meant, since Pu'er has more than one village of this name.
description:
Bangwai is a village in Fudong, Lancang County, in Pu'er prefecture, and its name reaches far beyond its output because of one tree. An old tea tree here is classed as a transitional type, sitting between wild and cultivated plants, and it made the village known to tea people.

The tea itself is handled the way sheng generally is: sun-dried maocha, then pressed or sold loose. Nothing specific to Bangwai is documented about the process, so its character has to come from the leaf and the place.

Drinkers describe it as firm and full with a wild edge, turning quickly from bitterness to sweetness and lasting a good number of steeps. Most of those descriptions come from sellers and enthusiasts, so read them as impressions. Short steeps with very hot water are a sensible start, as with other young sheng.

When buying, ask for the county as well as the name. Lancang's Bangwai is the one with the famous tree, but Jingdong County has villages called Bangwai too, and a cake from the famous tree itself is not what an ordinary Bangwai label means.
history:
The Bangwai transitional tree stands at about 1,900 m near the Lancang River, is 11.8 m tall and is commonly given an age of over a thousand years. Villagers still pick from it. Its botanical interest, alongside the quality of the local tea, is what raised the name.

Little else is documented about the village's tea trade, and no clear account of when its tea first sold under its own name has been established.
